newsitem.title: GERMANY: German private TV stations boost '96 ad income.
newsitem.headline: German private TV stations boost '96 ad income.

text.p: German private television stations, paced by the rising popularity of new cable channels, saw revenues climb 14 percent in 1996 while other media segments endured almost flat growth, research showed on Tuesday.

Private broadcasting was led by the RTL2 channel, which saw advertising sales jump 27.8 percent to 589 million marks ($363.2 million), and ProSieben, whose sales rose 18 percent to 2.35 billion marks, research group Nielson S+P said.
Combined, the nine private TV stations tracked by Nielsen generated sales of 9.82 billion marks -- or 39 percent of Germany's 25.16 billion mark media market.
In contrast, print media -- including newspapers, consumer magazines and trade publications -- revenues climbed a meagre 1.1 percent to 12.8 billion marks.
The two public television stations, ARD and ZDF, saw revenues rise 1.8 percent to 948 million marks, while radio sales slipped 0.9 percent to 1.576 billion.

RTL, controlled by publisher Bertelsmann, ranked as the top private broadcaster with 3.22 billion marks in sales, up 12 percent from 1995. Competitor SAT1, which is owned by the Kirch Group and Axel Springer Verlag AG, was second with 2.59 billion marks, up 3.8 percent.
New channel VOX collected 301 million marks, up 69 percent.
